utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone in this courtroom and those just outside. Mr. Stewart, before I ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom, in the beginning of the week you said you would think you would need the week for the cross-examination of Mr. Treanor. Does that mean that you expect to finish today?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do. It's going to be -- it's going to be fairly tight, as it often is, touch and go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then just get started. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Cross-examination will now be continued by Mr. Stewart. Mr. Stewart, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, could you have, please, Volume 4 of your bundles. And we're going to tab 62. And if we go to page 2, the foot of the page, item 2 on the agenda. Just remind us. We looked at this briefly yesterday, the agenda. Proposed recommendation, decision on the establishment of Municipal Assemblies of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And then if we go on to page 9. I had asked you in relation to a point, then -- the discussion begins on page 9. And then on point 10 -- I'm sorry, page 10, I had asked you whether the paragraph about four or five down, "Group of deputies," and so on, was broadly the same as Variant B, first level, paragraph 4. And then we ran into a little bit of choppy water because of some confusion over wording. But I think we cleared that up. When we go to -- on to page 12, we've got Dr. Karadzic talking. And towards the top of the page there's a paragraph beginning "In the army." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: "In the army there really are different tendencies. But on the part of individuals it's really not an official position. There are people cherishing different stupid ideas, but god willing that we stay the state everyone will go to the elections afterwards."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, whenever you start reading, your speed goes up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: "And take his chances there." On this issue and in other issues, again, this was certainly, wasn't it, Mr. Treanor, a session of considerable debate, wasn't it, this session of the Serb Assembly? It was very far from being a rubber-stamping meeting at which everybody just went along to endorse without serious discussion. It was a really rocky, tough debate, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can recall there was quite a bit of discussion and difference of opinion about the recommendation that we were just considering.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And we -- we've already dealt with it -- I think Mr. Krajisnik, so I won't repeat it -- at page 14, you had highlighted where Mr. Krajisnik explained and drawn attention to distinction between the regionalisation and the formation of municipal assemblies. So we won't simply go over the same ground again. But over at page 15, Mr. Krajisnik, again: "Please can we explain some things." And Mr. Krajisnik says -- do you see in the middle of the page: "The Serbian people have through their deputies"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. "The Serbian people have through their deputies formed the Assembly of the Serbian People in BH for one reason only, because through us here the will was imposed on our people. I am referring to the platform and memorandum, the disruptions of constitutionality. In a word, decisions were imposed which are contrary to the interests of the Serbian people. Similar decisions are made in various municipalities where our representatives are in the minority. To enable them to counter the irregular practices imposed by the SDA and the HDZ, we think that we should recommend that in such milieus where our representatives are in the minority, they can form Assemblies like this one here and fight with all means for their interests. "Let us -- let me explain what we can do. In municipalities such as Novi Grad, Hadzici, Stari Grad, et cetera, we have no rights whatever -0 whatsoever. It is there that Assemblies of the Serbian People should be formed, for by working in the Joint Assembly our representatives are only a front while the others are working and implementing decisions about which they ask none of the Serb representatives. That's the gist of the matter. In any case, I do not mind if we do not adopt this, but the initiative has come from numerous municipalities which claim that the representatives cannot achieve everything" -- -- anything - I beg your pardon, "anything," not everything -- -- "that everything is being done by outvoting and the will of others imposed on them. That way we are imposing our will on them too, I must admit, but representatives of the Serb people are in question here." So would you agree, Mr. Treanor, it could -- in fact, it could hardly have been more clearly explained and emphasised by Mr. Krajisnik at this point that the problem they were addressing related specifically to those municipalities where the Serbs were in a minority in the Assembly and were simply being outvoted?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And those -- and Novi Grad, Hadzici, Stari Grad, those are examples of that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Then when we go over to page 16, Mr. Krajisnik's talking again, the middle of the page: "In places where we can have no political influence on the life and work of the municipalities," and so on. So it's the same point. And then at the bottom of the page: "Let me be clear on this point. I am in favour of this, but tell --" a deputy. I beg your pardon. This is a deputy. He's not named. "Let me be clear on this point. I am in favour of this. But tell me, what do we gain with this new idea that Serbian deputies in those municipalities where they are a minority should be proclaimed and again vested with some powers with which they can achieve nothing? We do not even know how those parts who have joined different municipalities will achieve their rights. And let me assure you, this is creating an impression of helplessness among the people. These representatives will not be able to do anything this way, and we are now pulling wool over their eyes to delude them that they will be able to do and achieve something which, frankly speaking, I doubt." Mr. Treanor, would it be a fair summary there to say that this particular deputy was saying, "Well, this is an empty gesture. It's actually not -- it's not going to make any practical difference. We'll set up this parallel assembly and it went make any difference because we won't be able to control things anyway"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he's saying here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then we get the decision at page 18. It's a decision -- it's a draft only in the sense that of course it's intended to apply generally to the relevant municipalities so that the name gets filled in when it's used. But at page 18, it's a pretty detailed and specific provision. And then if we go on to -- so the decision has been set out. The -- what actually seems to happen is that -- yes, I beg your pardon. We go on to paragraph -- page 22. Mr. Krajisnik, towards the bottom, the chairman, that's Mr. Krajisnik, states: "It's evident that we either do not understand each other or fail to grasp the problems in the municipalities where we're in the minority. In our discussions, we all proceed from the situation in the area from which we come. Gentlemen, there are urban areas where we cannot resolve this by regionalisation because regionalisation is a completely separate issue. Now, we have Municipal Assemblies with three parties. They also have groups of deputies just like we here in the republic have with decisions constantly being adopted by the Assemblies. Rajko is mentioning regionalisation. I would like to ask that we discuss that when the time comes." And then you've highlighted this passage before. So going to the last sentence of this paragraph: "This is not in collision with regionalisation." So it appears Mr. Krajisnik, as no doubt often happens to somebody chairing a meeting, he's having to struggle a bit to get this point across, isn't he, to some of the deputies?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then he says: "Please do not make judgements proceeding from your municipalities where the Serbs are in the majority and where regional linking is possible." And then the next paragraph: "This will fit in in regional terms, and there is no problem in turning this into the Assembly of the Serbian People. That would be in our favour." And then there's a deputy, Mr. Jakic [phoen], says in the middle of the page: "I should like to make another remark. We said act, recommendation. Terminologically, a recommendation implies no obligation. Accordingly, this does not mean that in every municipality where we do not have a majority we have to form a Serb Assembly. What use is a Serb Assembly where you have two or three representatives?" So whether that's the same or a different deputy from the unnamed deputy earlier, it's -- in effect it's the same objection, isn't it, Mr. Treanor? What's the point, he's saying.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the point here is a little bit different. The other deputy was indicating that if an Assembly was set up consisting of however many members, what difference would that make? This deputy is suggesting that there are some places where -- and the example he seems -- he gives seems to indicate that his thought is where there are so few representatives that it wouldn't make any sense at all to even set up an Assembly. And if -- well, I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I accept that distinction. It's -- so in each case, it's practical futility, really, as -- of the proposal is -- the gist of what is being said in opposition, or in doubting the proposal.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In broad terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then we get a -- at page 24 a supplement being suggested to the decision, and it's of Mr. Radomir Neskovic, page 24, under a heading with his name. "I would like to suggest a supplement to this decision to form an Assembly of the Serbian People in the municipality and additionally that the Assembly assess the situation in its municipalities, taking into account all the specific features and propose to this Assembly what should be done there." And then he makes comment on regionalisation. Then he goes on: "In municipalities where we are in the minority, where we cannot exercise our power in any way because we're outvoted, I would suggest that the Assembly of the Serbian People when decisions are adopted inform the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina of that and that the Assembly, the Serbian People of BH, decide that, for instance, it will not recognise the decision of a given Municipal Assembly, for example of Zavidovici, if it endangers the interests of the Serbs." And then at page 26, Mr. Djurovic says: "Mr. President, from the moment this issue was introduced, I've been thinking about the effectiveness of the decisions we will adopt in these municipalities which do not have a majority Serb population. Believe me, I cannot imagine, knowing the organisational set-up of municipalities, a decision to be implemented in the area of such a municipality." And then Mr. Skoko, I think it is, at the foot of the page: "As for the municipalities, I fail to see what good will come out of creating Serbian municipal assemblies within municipalities where Serbs are outvoted and less-important organs which will implement these decisions are formed. What does the adoption of a decision at the municipal level mean if there are no organs of power to enforce it? It's a decision which is not binding on anyone; can just be just a proclamation without any chance of being implemented." And then in the middle of the page, Mr. Krajisnik is trying to steer deputies off discussing what the Muslims will do by saying: "Well, they don't ask us, so we won't worry about what they're doing in this area. That's a paraphrase. And then above the middle of the page, he says: "We suggest that we do so in places where we are in the minority; namely, see whether we will form municipalities or not. Nothing else." And then he asks if the supplement proposed by Mr. Neskovic, back at 24, which was to inform the BH Serb Assembly and get its support as necessary should be incorporated. The deputies say no. Then the chairman emphasises: "We should make sure of the following, that decisions adopted by representatives of municipalities and verified by this Assembly are not in collision with regionalisation and in the interests of regionalisation can we adopt this." The deputies say it can't be adopted. It's a bit confusing. That seems to be the Neskovic proposal at this point, isn't it, that's being rejected, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then in the middle of page 28: "The Assembly agreed to adopt such a decision with the following supplement, that it is recommended to groups of deputies of the SDS Municipal Assemblies in BH on whom decisions contrary to the interests of the Serbian people are imposed, to have the decisions of groups of deputies to transform themselves into Assemblies of the Serbian People verified by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina." So is it a fair summary that a bit of Mr. Neskovic's proposed supplement actually did get into the final decision?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would seem so. I'm not -- I guess that would depend on the technical meaning of the word "verified," but it would certainly seem so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So as I suggested to you, Mr. Treanor, and you agreed, we can see that there was -- there was serious debate about this issue, but it all, all, proceeded only in relation to those municipalities where the Serbs were in a minority and were therefore liable simply to be outvoted.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And that recommendation was published. Now, in the -- if we go to the document -- I think we can put that on one side, that file, if that's convenient for you. And if we then go to the document which is at 6/66, Volume 6, tab 66, which is the Variant A and B document. If we look at the preamble first, turning over the cover page. And then we get a preamble before we come to the heading "Variant A." It's item 3 of the preamble: "The tasks, measures, and other activities from these instructions are carried out on the whole territory of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, in all municipalities where the Serbs live. And this is completely in municipalities where the Serb people are in majority," Variant A; "partially in municipalities where the Serb people are not in majority," Variant B. So if this was, Mr. Treanor, if this were to have been distributed in accordance with its terms in that paragraph, it would have gone to presidents of every single -- the Serb -- the Serb leaders in every municipality throughout the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would presume that this document would have gone to the presidents of the SDS in every municipality where the SDS was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. I beg your pardon. The presidents of the SDS Municipal Boards in -- wherever there was one.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Throughout the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We would in that situation, if this was a clear, express instruction to be implemented immediately, we would have expected, wouldn't we, to have seen widespread implementation of these instructions within a relatively short period, wouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the end of the instructions, it says that -- something to the effect that they're to be implemented when the appropriate order is given.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So the places -- I'm sorry, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't know -- for one thing, we don't know the nature of what order may have been given in regard to the implementation, on the one hand. On the other, we do see implementation beginning, as I mentioned earlier, as soon as the 23rd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, it may be, Mr. Treanor, that we are already, as far as this is concerned, in an area of evidence which is really for other witnesses, rather than for you, which is the actual practical implementation what happened in municipalities. So I'll just ask you: Are you aware of any such a signal to implement these recommendations having been communicated to anybody in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as we indicated in the report in the paragraphs that you referred to yesterday - I believe paragraph 61 and 62 - in discussing these instructions, we reached a tentative conclusion that the instructions were distributed on the 20th of December at a meeting, at which time presumably the order was also given to implement them. What the nature of the order was, we don't know. Based on the documents, we can only infer that it had something to do with actually implementing these instructions, since we see them being implemented soon after that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, that's really what I was getting at, tying in with your answer a few minutes ago. When you made a reference to provisions at the end of the document - and "provisions" is my word - but you made a reference. You were talking, I take it, particularly about the very last two numbered items before we get to the reference to the SDS Crisis Staff, numbers 3 and 4 at the very end of the document in English, beginning, number 3, "the tasks, measures," and number 4, "a secret procedure."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's what you were talking about. So that the three -- these instructions, in a nutshell, can be applied only on the order of the president of the SDS in Bosnia and Herzegovina according, to a secret procedure. And then, 4: "Providing for the secret procedure to be established later." The point of what I was asking you earlier, Mr. Treanor, was -- I said well, if they -- if this document, as on its face it appears to have been, was designed to go to the presidents of the SDS Municipal Boards, wherever they existed throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, I suggested to you that it was therefore surprising if it really did that it wasn't much more widely implemented. And your response to that was, I think, along the lines of, "Well, it didn't fall to be implemented until the signal was given in accordance with those provisions at the end of the document." Have I summarised what you said at that point sufficiently accurately?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, then, are you aware of any such signal having been given to those -- that limited number of municipalities where evidence has been given that there was implementation of at least some provisions of this document in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again -- as I think I said already, presuming that our inference is correct that these instructions were distributed in some fashion on the 20th of December, we don't know whether on the basis of the documents certainly that we adduced in the report, whether on that occasion it was distributed to every Municipal Board, and we don't know what the order, as referred to here at the end in paragraph 3, what the order of the president on that occasion may have been. Obviously it could have been anything from please implement this in every municipality, and here's a copy for everyone, to, for instance, let's only implement this now in these particular municipalities or only in Variant A municipalities or Variant B municipalities, or something of that description. I just don't know, on the basis of the documents that we had available in the report and, indeed, documents which I'm aware of now. The document from Bratunac that we referred to in those paragraphs makes -- to me, makes it clear that the president of the SDS in Bratunac received these instructions on that occasion and went back to Bratunac and sought to implement them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But whether, again, the others insofar as they may not have done that didn't do that because they were too lazy or too incompetent to do so or whether they were not told to do so at that time or whether we just don't have records of what they did, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, for such an apparently - and this is the way it's presented by the Prosecution in this case - for such an apparently very important document, Mr. Treanor, the degree of laziness which led to all the municipalities apart from a very small number, simply not bothering to do anything about it at that point in December would have been extraordinary, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't qualify it one way or another. I think that Dr. Karadzic perceived that there were some -- a slowness about this. And there are references later on, indeed I believe into March, of the necessity for doing this. So there apparently was some slowness about doing so, for whatever reason. There may have been other reasons in the discussion during the Third Session of the Assembly that we were just referring to, the discussion relating to the recommendation to set up Serbian Assemblies in the municipalities. I believe at least one of the deputies expressed reluctance to do so because he felt that that would exacerbate relations between the SDS and the other parties in that municipality rather senselessly, since he seemed to feel that there was some possibility there of them, in fact, all coming to an agreement, so that such a step would sabotage his efforts to, I think as he put it, to win over that whole municipality, and so therefore he did not want to split it. Now, that is one reason, I believe, why the December 11th document was couched as a recommendation. I think I indicated this yesterday. That was only a recommendation. And I believe that was one of the reasons. This document is not recommendation. It's an instruction to be implemented at the order of the president of the SDS, whereas the other document, again, was a recommendation from the Assembly of the Serbian People.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any material to suggest that it was contemplated that the triggering procedure in those paragraphs 3 and 4 at the end of this document was proposed to be on a selective basis, municipality by municipality or by batches of municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I'm only suggesting that as a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Mr. Treanor. Yes. Let's look at Variant A, which is on page 2 of the document and particularly first level, paragraph 4. It says: "An Assembly --" sorry, I'll give everybody a moment. It's the top of page 3, very top of page 3, item 4: "An Assembly of the Serb People in the municipality is to be called and proclaimed, which will be made up of the representatives of the Serb people in the Municipal Assembly." Mr. Treanor, what could have been the point of such a provision in a municipality where the Serbs were in the majority in the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite frankly, I could only speculate on that. I think I share your puzzlement as to why that is in there, and I believe I am correct in saying, although I am speaking from memory and incomplete documentation on this, that as far as we know no such Assembly was ever formed in a Variant A municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sir, I think, very fairly acknowledging that you share my forensic puzzlement, Mr. Treanor, in a nutshell, is the answer that there isn't in fact any rational explanation for the instruction in paragraph 4, first level of Variant A?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I could only speculate on that. I'm -- as I said, I do not understand why it's in here. Maybe there was the thought that maybe we should have our own Assembly so we can conduct our own business without the other deputies who we -- to be sure can outvote. They won't even know what we're doing. Maybe there was some thought like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I understand, Mr. Treanor, your -- you very frankly expressed your puzzlement to begin with. So as I'm pressing you, you are, as you very fairly say, speculating as to what it could possibly be. May I suggest to you, acknowledging that I don't think you put forward that speculation with huge enthusiasm for it, it appears, that there's not a hint of any such usefulness of this provision in the debate in the Assembly that we looked at earlier this morning, is there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And actually, since in that debate it's also fair to say, isn't it, that the explanation given, I think by Mr. Krajisnik - but if I'm wrong about that, it probably doesn't matter very much - but the explanation given was, well, look, what we're really proposing in this recommendation is that on a municipal level you do what we've done on the BH level, which is because we were being outvoted it was simply essential for us to set up our own Assembly.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So if we take that - I don't want to press it too painfully - but if we take that analogy, that would have been as if the Serbs on the BH level, even able to achieve a minority in the -- a majority in the BH Assembly and therefore, of course, control things, said, "Well, actually, we'd like to have our own Assembly."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And if we go on to the second level of Variant A, paragraph 1: "A session of the Serb --" I'm sorry. I'll give everyone a moment. It's the very top of page 4: "A session of the Serb Municipal Assembly is to be called. A Municipal Executive Board is to be formed and municipal governmental organs are to be created," and so on. It's effectively the same point, Mr. Treanor. So I won't belabour it too much, but again, there was no need, was there, for the Serbs in municipalities where they were in a majority to form a Municipal Executive Board because they controlled the one that was already in existence?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And again, the only point here that I can see would be that on that Executive Board, as in the Assembly, there may have been representatives of other parties. So the desire here may have been to form a purely Serbian executive body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It may be too broad a question for you, Mr. Treanor, in which case please say so, but knowing what you know about this time, this place, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the situation, what is your comment on the suggestion that that would have been an extremely foolish political step to take because you would be substituting for a situation in which you democratically controlled the proper, democratically appointed organ while having a minority there who could democratically express their view but whom you could consistently outvote, you would be replacing that with an organ about which there would - I'll use the word "inevitably" here - be considerable consternations and objections to its legitimacy and it would be said, "Well, you're just -- you're just walking over us now, because you've excluded us even from the debate." So you would give yourself all the negative aspects of creating a body of doubtful legitimacy in others' eyes but not actually improved your ability to get through decisions and do what you want. It's a rather long question, but I'm sure you got that point, Mr. Treanor. It would be foolish politics, wouldn't it, to do that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This discussion is very hypothetical, since I'm not aware that this ever happened. However, the point in regard to the Executive Board or the Executive Committee, as we, I think, tend to refer to the governmental bodies, not to confuse them with the party boards, the point is that the Executive Committee was composed of the heads of the various administrative departments of the municipality, and as heads of the departments, they had their own authority within those departments. As a result of the election -- the elections in 1990 and the interparty agreement that was reached, the distribution of the places on municipal executive boards was to be in some fashion proportional to the strength of the various -- of the three national parties who were in the coalition, was to be proportional to their strength in the Municipal Assembly, so that members of the HDZ or the SDA could have been and probably were in fact in control of certain of the executive organs of municipalities which were Serbian majority municipalities even. So there may have been a desire to have a, as I put it, a purely Serbian executive in order to be ready to get control of the individual departments that may not already have been controlled by the SDS. So it's not simply a question of voting within the Executive Committee, but there's also an issue of the control of the municipal administrative organs. Again, this is all extremely hypothetical and speculative as to why this provision may be in here, a provision which I'm not aware was ever implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Treanor, I can comment that the hypothesis in question is to some extent one you had floated yourself in an earlier answer. What -- and we're looking at Variant A at the moment -- what Variant A contemplated was - and we see this in first level, number 5, at page 3 - that "As well as the calling and proclaiming of what would be this new Assembly, in fact, the Serb Assembly, that in fact preparations were to be made for the formation of municipal state organs, an Executive Board -" it sounds a bit repetitive there -"administrative organs, magistrates, courts," and so on. So the whole system that you've described of the existing Executive Board, where perhaps posts of heads of different departments would be allocated among the parties, that would effectively be gone, wouldn't it, under the -- what's contemplated in paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what would have been gone?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's -- paragraph 5, as at the Bosnia-Herzegovina level -- paragraph 5 in Variant A first level, it contemplates parallel organs, doesn't it, within the municipality?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, the difference between level -- what are we calling it -- the first level and the second level seems to be basically one between preparations on the first level and actually carrying out things on the second level.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. It's not in fact as clear-cut as that, is it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, broadly speaking, I mean, that's the difference between the two levels, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In your report at paragraph 64 - and you've confirmed this in your evidence. The transcript reference is 1574 - you said that the -- paragraph 64 it is. It's actually just a short passage. You said: "The signal to activate the second stage of preparations anticipated in the 19th December 1991 instructions was given by Karadzic on the 14th of February, 1992 at yet another expanded Deputies' Club session on the day before the Seventh Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly." When you talk about the signal to activate the second stage of preparations, just -- can we just be clear as to what you mean by "the second stage."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the second stage, referring to what is described in this document as the second level, and where in other places and perhaps in my testimony I refer to as the second degree. In this -- in the A and B document, we have Variants A and B and we have first level, first degree, first stage, second stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So does that imply, therefore, if the -- well, let me start with a prior question. Those paragraphs at the very end of the document, paragraphs 3 and 4, "The tasks, measures and other activities in these instruction cans only be applied only on the order of the president of the SDS in BH," it clearly doesn't in terms provide for instructions or the triggering order of the president to be given in stages. Just taking it bit by bit, step by step, it doesn't in terms say that. That's clear, isn't it, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- no, it doesn't lay that out. I would have thought that was the implication, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Treanor, going on to say that of course equally it certainly doesn't rule it out and in practice. I'm not going to suggest that you -- that you can't, then, follow what's contemplated by 3 and 4 by giving the triggering order in stages. I'm not suggesting that to you. But your suggestion in that paragraph of your report that on the 14th of February Mr. Karadzic gave the signal to activate the second stage implies, doesn't it, that at some point the signal was given to activate the first stage?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And -- but I think perhaps it's already clear that it's really, as far as you're concerned, it's a complete mystery as to when and how any such signal to activate the first stage might have been given.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I have said here and we've said in the report that the -- it would appear that the first stage was ordered, implemented beginning on the 20th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I think -- well, I don't want to go over old ground there. The first stage would have been -- so that the thesis, if you like - whether it's a thesis or a hypothesis here, but I'd say that it's a thesis - is that the instructions to implement the first stage, either they were given very selectively to a small number of municipalities or they were very largely not carried out in a wide number of municipalities. That's the position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the degree to which they were carried out is not entirely known to us, because we don't have documentation from every single municipality, at least not that I'm aware of. So the precise degree of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. implementation is not known. It would appear from later statements even after the 14th of February by Dr. Karadzic that in fact it had not been carried out; in some places even by that late date. So there certainly does seem to have been some variance in the implementation of the instructions. And let me comment and perhaps draw attention to the obvious that this is a bit of a murky area. The documentation on it is by no means complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And perhaps we can go, then, and have a look at the intercepts bundle, because you've dealt with this point. I may have already given the page reference. You were dealing with this at page 1579. It is in the transcript of your evidence earlier. And you -- at that point in your evidence you had been referring to an item from the transcripts bundle. It's item 27 -- it's tab 27, and it's page 5 of the English transcript, and it was at a session of the Main and Executive Board of the SDS on the 14th of February, the date you've given. And he says about halfway down the page, just below halfway down: "The main attitude towards Yugoslavia during this entire interfering of the European Community was that the Serbs were right but the factual situation is so and so -- was so and so. Now we are in the position to say yes, maybe the Muslims are right but the fact of the situation is so and so - although they're not right - the factual situation is so and so. Now it is so. Now it's up to us. It's up to each individual to do his part of the job. We shall also talk about that today, but I have to say that we must be wise, unified, dedicated in order to take the last drop of power into our hands in a humane way, of course carry it out in a humane way, a just way towards both Muslims and Croats who live there. That is particularly important that there would be no fleeing from our areas. But also that a bird cannot come in without your knowledge. That is, if you remember; who keeps that in mind or maybe not on his person a stage number 2. There is, remember -- you know what I'm talking about. We know -- yes. That is therefore the stage number 2, the second stage in smaller or bigger variations, but you have to implement that slowly now to have absolute control who is travelling along your roads, what they are transporting, for which purposes. That's the way it must be. You have to have at your disposal," and so on. And that's what you get or that's where you get the reference to the Variant A and B instructions and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And what I suggest is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you are asked to speak more into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's where you get the reference to the Variant A and B instructions and that's where you get the signal from Mr. Karadzic to implement stage 2. That's right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think there's at least one more reference to that matter in this document. And this document may not be a complete record of what transpired on that particular day or indeed on that particular weekend, which saw more than one meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Are you pointing the Trial Chamber to some other specific reference, then, in the documentation that we do have to support this point?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought I had in my testimony. Maybe I didn't. But I think there is at least one more reference to the second degree, second level in this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It may be helpful if I direct everyone's attention to page 17 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tieger has very helpfully directed us to page 17, but now we are in page 17 I think I have to invite you, Mr. Treanor, to indicate what you might suggest on page 17 supports this point.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the middle of the page, I can see beginning at line 14, "There is nothing that we shall disapprove of except for foolish things, and I think that we, Serbs, must stop with declarations -- with declaration. We've had enough declarations. And now these declarations should be translated into a map. And the stage number 2 should also be converted, the one we've talked about, the one you have, if not here, then at home, in order to have authorities in the field functioning, that a bird cannot fly over really," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So that's the point you had in mind, is it, Mr. Treanor, a few minutes ago when you said there was another reference in this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I thought there was at least one more reference, and there's one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's -- I suggest to you this is an extremely -- you could only work with the documents you got, but it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Since we are also working with this document, I would suggest turning to page 24. Mr. Treanor has also indicated other references, and that would be found -- sorry -- also in the middle of the page, approximately line 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Page 24, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Page 24, Mr. Treanor. The reference -- well, clearly: "What is in mind is as regards the essence of which Mr. Radic spoke. Now, please, that's why we called you today, to intensify, to introduce the second level, and to intensify the functioning of the government at any cost and on every single millimetre of our territory."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, as I -- and I will check now if the Court would like me to, but I believe I indicated in my --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, you --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- direct testimony that the expression being used here is the -- in Serbian is the same as in the original Variant A/Variant B document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The expression -- the first phrase "level,"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The level --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Level. It's -- well, in English, Mr. Treanor, but perhaps you can say whether the position is different in Serbian, in English I'd suggest to you this is an extremely flimsy basis on which to link what Mr. Karadzic is saying on the 14th of February with this specific document bearing the date 19th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I don't want to characterise it in any particular fashion. I have indicated it here, and I have also indicated that this is a rather murky area. Documentation is scanty. But I believe, based on the language being used and the context of what's being said, and specifically, for instance, the reference to control, that the reference here is to the same document; that is to say, to the Variant A and B document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You see, I suggest there are two different things. If you -- one is where you start from the position that such a document exists, has the official endorsement of the SDS in December 1991, is distributed with the approval or possibly even under the direction of Dr. Karadzic, then perhaps linking slightly murky or flimsy words with that is not as difficult a task --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe this is a question attempting to elicit information. I think this is argument. And I think it's gone too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I haven't finished it yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But I think Mr. Tieger said that it tended to be an argument. That's how I understood his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I heard what he said, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You finish your question, and then we'll decide whether we'll allow the witness to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But, Mr. Treanor, I suggest if you start from -- you're the expert assessing all these things on the basis of the documentation you've seen. If you start from the position that this document did not have the official approval of the SDS leadership, did not in fact come officially from an organ of the SDS party in December 1991, then I suggest to you that you would not have found enough in the words of the record of the 14th of February, 1991 to link what Dr. Karadzic was saying with any confidence at all to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does your objection still stand, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. It's slightly different. I think the way this question was framed, I might add, it seems to me to emphasise that my earlier objection was well founded. However, now it's veered into the realm of speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may answer the question, Mr. Treanor. Perhaps you could reread it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have been reading it, Your Honour. I take it to mean, basically, that if the document didn't exist would I think that it was being referred to on February the 14th. The answer to that is no. Quite logically, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the starting point of the question was not whether the document exists but whether it was approved and adopted, I think you said. Did not have the official approval of the SDS leadership, did not come officially from an organ, which, of course, is not exact through same as the existence of a document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, okay, if it didn't exist in terms of the party, if there was no -- if there was no such instruction current within the party, then clearly there couldn't be a reference to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one additional question: Is the fact that "second level" is between quotation marks, does that -- first of all, does that appear in the original?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On which page, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On page 24. It says: "To intensify, to introduce the second level." "Second level" appears in the English text in quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In quotation marks. Yes, I see that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that have any -- as far as giving specific to the wording here? I mean it's -- "second level" could be a very abstract concept related to whatever could be on the second level. Is it of any significance to you that "second level" here is between quotation marks when interpreting the meaning of this part of the words spoken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would have to refresh my memory as to whether it was used in the original. If it were used in the original here or elsewhere, it could -- one conclusion could be that it was considered to be some sort of term of art that had a particular meaning. But again, whether it actually is used in quotation marks in the original and whether it's done so consistently and whether that is or is not a peculiarity of the transcriber, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that type of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't attach undue significance to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Extreme significance to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In your report at paragraph 62, you say -- I think perhaps -- I read the first sentence a short while ago, but you go on then, the second sentence: "Given the nature of the document" -- this Variant A and B document -- "many municipal leaders must also have been summoned to the session if only" - that's in Sarajevo - "if only as it appears to be," excuse me, "informed about what to do next. It is significant that these detailed and wide-ranging written instructions from the SDS leadership were apparently ready for dissemination when the larger group was convened. Although the circumstances surrounding the distribution of the 19th December 1991 instructions cannot be fully reconstructed from available documents, it seems evident that any Main Board meeting on this issue on 20th of December was simply an occasion to disseminate already agreed, prepared, and drafted measures." Just pausing at that point. You say "it seems evident that any Main Board meeting on this issue on 20th of December was simply an occasion to disseminate already agreed, prepared, and drafted measures." So it's inherent in what you're saying there that you're assuming a Main Board meeting which was summoned apparently for the purposes, at least primarily, of dealing with this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you -- is it correct you don't actually have any -- you don't have any material that you've seen that enables you to draw any reliable conclusion that a Main Board meeting on 20th December took place primarily to deal with this issue?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time this was written, we -- we had used the documents which are indicated in the footnotes, which refer to there being a meeting, having been a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. But --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Footnote 183, "running from municipality to municipality." And we simply put that together with the date of the document itself and the initiation of the implementation. To conclude, as it says at the beginning of the paragraph, "It is most likely on available evidence that the document was distributed a session of the Main Board on 20 December 1991." Let me remark that this section of the report is about decision-making within the SDS and perhaps not, rather -- perhaps not elegantly enough, what this paragraph is saying inter alia is that we really don't know anything about how this document was formulated or adopted. The only thing that we've been able to discover is when it may have been distributed. Now, since this report was written, additional documentation has come to our attention, for example, in the form of telephone conversations, one of which I believe I used in my presentation in which reference is made apparently to this meeting. I'm citing from memory now. I believe it was the telephone conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Novakovic on the 18th or 19th of December at which Dr. Karadzic refers to a meeting the next day and indicates something about the nature of the meeting which connects with this document. Again, I can't remember the exact details, because there was another telephone conversation as well that I didn't use that points in the same direction, a telephone conversation with -- between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Risto Djogo about at the same time that contains similar references.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There just -- there seems, I suggest to you - would you agree - that there's an element of circularity in your approach in order to be reaching the conclusion that the meeting of the Main Board was called on this issue or primarily on this issue. You're using as support for that the existence of the document itself with the date of the 19th of December.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, have I said the meeting dealt primarily with this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, "primarily" was my word, but your report talked about, in the middle of paragraph 62, you're saying "it seems evident," which I understand in effect to be an expressed view therefore by you. "It seems evidence that any Main Board meeting on this issue on the 20th of December was simply an occasion to disseminate." So perhaps we can clarify this. I had taken it that the phrase "any Main Board meeting on this issue" meant either a Main Board meeting to deal only with this issue or - and I took the lesser of the two - a Main Board meeting primarily dealing with this issue. Do you see, Mr. Treanor? Because otherwise, I'm suggesting, if it's just one of a number of issues, it's not aptly described as a Main Board meeting on this issue.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the point of the sentence is that we do not think that the document itself was discussed and adopted on that occasion in the manner at which documents were discussed and adopted, for instance, at the Assembly. The document is dated the 19th of December. We know from the diary that there was a meeting on the 20th of December, a meeting of the Main Board. There was a meeting of the Main Board on the 20th. There was then a meeting of the Assembly on the 21st, the 22nd was a Sunday, and the first time the implementation of instructions appear on Monday the 23rd. Therefore, basically on that sequence of events we have made the tentative -- what I would call tentative conclusion, since buttressed by additional evidence, that it is most likely that the document was distributed at a session of the Main Board on the 20th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a suitable break point for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It would be. We'll adjourn until five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Treanor, I checked back in the transcript as to what you'd said about that conversation on the 19th of December, 1991 between Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Novakovic and, actually, in the light of what you said in your evidence in chief I don't need to pursue it in cross-examination. What you -- we were looking at paragraph 62 of your report. And what you had said after the sentence that I've just before referring to about the meeting on this issue on the 20th of December, the next sentence was then: "Given all the proceeding, furthermore, it is likely that some informal group or body within the top SDS leadership had determined the policy based upon which this document was drafted for dissemination to a wider circle of SDS loyalists and subsequently implemented throughout BH." And so far as the suggestion that it was some informal group or body was concerned, though not being entirely sure whether you personally can offer any more on the topic, Mr. Treanor, I am putting to you so that it can be clear to everybody, and particularly the Trial Chamber, what the case is, was that this document was indeed prepared by an informal group or body but not a body technically within the top SDS leadership; that was it was in fact prepared by, I'd say, some group, because that's the most I can say, of retired military officers and was never, in fact, an official or officially adopted or endorsed document of the SDS party. Can you -- I'm putting that case. It may be, Mr. Treanor, that there is no further comment you can offer beyond what you've already said. But if you can, please do.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You made reference to a group of Yugoslav army officers, which is interested. We at a certain point in time - and I'm not sure when that was - we sent a request for assistance to the authorities of Republika Srpska in connection with this document. I can't remember the exact terms of the request, but it was basically seeking information on the background to the document. And we received a reply from the central office of the SDS, I believe, saying that they didn't really know anything about it -- but maybe they didn't say that, because they said they knew something about it -- that the only information they had was that there may have been some group of retired army officers who drafted it or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. That's absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In fact, I have the -- that particular letter or I think it would be that particular letter in front of me, that Mr. Blewitt, Graham Blewitt, deputy prosecutor, had written to the liaison officer for the Republika Srpska, that being the liaison this institution, this Tribunal, and the Republika Srpska. And the reply received had, as well as information about what happened to documents. Mr. Blewitt was inquiring about whether -- about distribution list for copies of Variant A and B document because a number of copies, as we know, were in the possession of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And the paragraph in question was: "The Main Board, as well as any other SDS body, never considered or instructed the organisation and activation of Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina at its sessions. We were informed that such instructions were given by a certain number of retired officers of the former Yugoslav People's Army." That's the letter and the passage that you had in mind --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- in your answer a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's an exchange of correspondence Mr. Blewitt wrote on the 30th of July, 2001, and so the reply from Republika Srpska from Milovan Bjelica was dated the 5th of November, 2001. In bundle 11, at tab 115, Mr. Treanor. We looked at this before for other purposes. Assembly of the -- the Serb Assembly, Fourteenth Session, 27th [Realtime transcript read in error: "29th"] of March, 1992 at page 23 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the session of the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, did it not say the 27th? I beg your pardon. Yes, I did say 29th. Thank you for correcting that. 27th. At page 23, just under halfway down this page, it's Dr. Karadzic speaking, and he says: "When we consider the overall situation, we do not see what they will gain by it. They can attempt to intimidate the Serbs here and there in Gorazde. They can kill someone in Brod, but they can never incorporate Serbian areas into their state or conquer them because they do not possess the forces required for the extensive territory held by the Serbs. We know that our people have armed themselves. We don't know the various ways and means by which this was done, but we do know that the people have enough weapons. I must say, however, that we do not have paramilitary units. When you return to your municipalities, especially the newly formed municipalities, I ask you to do what you are required and entitled to do under the law. The moment you arrive in your municipalities, you must urgently establish Crisis Staffs. You must try to organise the people so that they can defend themselves. Find a number of reserve officers for those staffs and have them register everyone who owns weapons as well as units. They should organise Territorial Defence and if the JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, is there, they must be placed under its command. If they're not, let them be placed under the command of reserve officers. They may not go anywhere but must remain in place to defend their territories," and so on. Mr. Treanor, in the light of your conclusions as to what had already happened in relation to Variants A and B, if it had been distributed in the way that you describe, at least some triggering of first level had occurred, and if Dr. Karadzic on the 14th of February had said something to trigger off the second level, why was this injunction in that passage necessary?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I referred to this earlier as an indication that Dr. Karadzic apparently felt that the instructions had not been carried out to an adequate degree in their entirety, and therefore on this occasion is repeating the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's an extremely mild exhortation, isn't it, by Dr. Karadzic for -- to deal with the situation of the failure to implement an instruction about which on your view of the matter a great deal of trouble had been taken. It had been specifically disseminated before the end of 1991. It is a very detailed document. It requires a large number of steps to be taken. And in circumstances where, apparently, it just largely hasn't been complied with, Dr. Karadzic is expressing himself in rather uncharacteristically mild terms, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you've called the terms you're using "mild" twice, which leads me to the thought, which quite frankly I didn't have before, that perhaps the extent of non-fulfilment wasn't really all that great and he was merely addressing himself to a few laggards. I really don't know. I mean, as I indicated earlier, this is a rather murky area and this is one of the things that makes it murky. One of the other things that makes it murky is the conversation of the -- with Mr. Novakovic on the 18th of December in which Mr. Karadzic already refers to the introduction of the second degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The same documents, if we go over -- I'm talking about those minutes of the Assembly on the 27th of March. If we go over to the next page, page 24 - 24 in English, 31 in the B/C/S version - first complete paragraph: "A war in Bosnia and Herzegovina will not solve anything. If it breaks out, you will get the plans. But I urge you to immediately organise the people within Territorial Defence units headed by reserve officers, form squads, platoons, and Crisis Staffs and engage retired officers. This must be done throughout our areas." Now, particularly the reference to "Crisis Staffs" there, Mr. Karadzic is saying, and obviously the breaking out of -- the outbreak of war is on the horizontal to say the least, but "you will get the plans." Then a specific reference to a number of matters to be dealt with, including Crisis Staffs. So what it comes to is you -- you will get plans, implying, I suggest, Mr. Treanor, some specific detail, because it will be war there. And he's saying, "But in the meantime, until that happens, until you get these detailed plans, "Do the following," and the following includes Crisis Staffs. Mr. Treanor, isn't that extremely difficult to reconcile with a situation in which Crisis Staffs themselves, then, have already been set up or instructions have already been given for that to be done some months previously?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite frankly, I think this passage is a little bit less problematic in that degree, if we grant that they had not been set up everywhere that Dr. Karadzic might have liked to have seen them set up, the reference to them in this speech seems to presume that everyone knows what a Crisis Staff is and what setting up a Crisis Staff entails.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, he does spell out in the next paragraph that "The presidents of municipalities and Executive Boards will hold the highest ranks in the Crisis Staff." He feels the need to spell out that absolutely simple, basic element, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he mentions that particular element, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But he wouldn't need to do that if everybody was already very familiar with a detailed formulation of the plans, would he?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the degree to which he may have wanted to address particular points, refresh people's memories, especially those that hadn't set up Crisis Staffs, was of course up to him within the framework of making his speech. As he indicated on the 14th of February, he realised that not everyone had that document under their arm on that particular occasion but, rather, may have had them at home, so particularly - and I'm just speculating - particularly for those that hadn't carried out the instruction, he's doing a bit of memory refreshing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Crisis Staff -- the concept of a Crisis Staff, it wasn't a completely new idea or new animal in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a rather obscure area as well. I believe the Presidency, the non-Serbian members of the Presidency had formed a Crisis Staff at a certain point in time. There may have been an HDZ Crisis Staff, but the -- at a high level, the central Crisis Staffs. We're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the earliest Crisis Staffs within the context of the conflicts that I'm aware of were in fact formed in Croatia by the authorities of the Republic of Croatia in the summer of 1991. So this was a term that was out there. And by the way, the Variant A and B document was published in the Bosnian press at the beginning of March 1992, so the idea of Serbian Crisis Staffs was also public. But the particular composition, duties, and activities of any particular so-called Crisis Staff would presumably have varied from place to place or from entity to entity, from party to party.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: With Crisis Staff, what I had in mind was it was a familiar term. It was a more widely used concept to -- Crisis Staffs could be formed in a whole range of emergency situations, floods and natural disasters.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have heard that, but I have never seen a document that that effect. And believe me, I have looked into the matter. Which doesn't mean that it is not correct, but I have only heard that and I have never seen a document to that effect. But as I have said, we have found out that the Republic of Croatia established Crisis Staffs in the -- at various levels in the summer of 1991, and we find that after that time that we see this. And indeed, Dr. Karadzic uses that term in the summer of 1991 in a telephone conversation, after -- Beginning with that period, the summer of 1991, we see this term being used in various contexts in connection with the conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then if -- if we look back at page 24, that same minutes of the Serb Assembly, the same paragraph we were looking at towards the top of the page, Mr. -- Dr. Karadzic continues after, according to you, reminding everybody that the presidents of municipalities and Executive Boards would hold the highest ranks in the Crisis Staff. The next sentence: "We must study the situation regarding the saving of lives, property, and territory. We have no other plans." Now, if we look back at the Variant A and B document, which, to remind ourselves is in bundle 6, the first tab numbered 66 - we probably don't need to grind through it in any great detail - but do you agree, Mr. Treanor, that the document itself contains quite a number of paragraphs and points which do relate to the saving or protection of lives and property? Let me give you an example. In Variant A, first level, paragraph 6: "The organisation of protection for important facilities in the municipality is to be strengthened." 7: "Control is to be established and a check carried out of existing material reserves." Paragraph 11: "Preparations are to be made for the protection of children, pregnant women, elderly people," so and so, "including preparations for protection and evacuation." Two bullet or dash points down: "The protection of resources is important for defence and resistance as well as for the life and the work of the population." So I could go on, as I sometimes do, Mr. Treanor. There's lots of -- lots in that document, isn't there, relating clearly to the saving - and I've added the word "protection" because I think that's the clear sense - saving and protection of lives and property?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. In fact, at the very beginning of the instructions, reference is made to the defence of the interests of the Serbian people, and that was certainly among their interests.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's just that where Dr. Karadzic says "we must study the situation regarding the saving of lives, property, and territory, we have no other plans," the obvious sense of that is we'll have to give -- excuse me. We will have to give you more details of that later. This is under review. This is under consideration. You will get the plans when the time comes, but we haven't yet done them. Isn't that the obvious sense of what he's saying?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's apparently referring to a set of plans. Whether he's referring to this set of plans or another set of plans, I don't know, because I haven't seen any other set of plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I do suggest on this particular question that you are really avoiding answering my question. So I urge you: Isn't it the obvious sense of what Dr. Karadzic is saying that they did not have formulated plans in relation to the saving of lives and property - that's under study, under consideration - and those will be provided at some point in the future?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have thought there was a contradiction between saying you'll get plans and then saying we don't have plans. I don't know what plans precisely he doesn't have. But beyond that, I mean, we're getting into a semantic issue, plans versus instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, we are not getting into a semantic issue. Referring to this as a semantic issue is not answering the question.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'll put it more shortly, then. It's clear that Dr. Karadzic is saying we haven't got plans ready for you on protection of lives and property, saving of lives and property, but you will get them when you need them.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that isn't clear to me. The comes -- the statement "we have no plans" comes at the end of a paragraph at which -- in which a number of things are alluded to. It could refer to any one of those. In -- it indeed may be referring to some additional plans that they want to have in -- regarding to saving lives and property.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's a source of scientific exercise that you're engaged in, Mr. Treanor. When we put these comments together with the puzzling point at the very beginning of all this as to what on earth Variant A was needed for so far as the setting up of new Assemblies of Serb People were concerned, doesn't it tend to lead much more probably to the conclusion that this was put together, the Variant A and B document, by some group, such as the Defence is saying, who did not think it through and had not worked it out and didn't have the political grasp of the situation that Dr. Karadzic and others associated with him would have had?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, are you able to answer the question on the probability of conclusions as suggested by Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think I would certainly agree, as we discussed Variant A, that it does not -- the document in its wording doesn't reveal -- indicate the type of concerns in regard to Variant A municipalities, if I can use that expression, that were or were not, as the case is, manifested at the 11 December session. I think the document is very much a Variant B document, if I can put it that way, that the important part of that document is really Variant B for the -- many of the reasons that we've already discussed here. So I would not say that the document was drafted by members of the Assembly, for instance, or Mr. Krajisnik, who was very sensitive to the differences between majority and minority municipalities. The only indication that we now -- that -- well, we didn't have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. any indication in the documents from that period as to who did draft that document, which we indicated. We've had a subsequent indication that it might have been drafted by a group of army officers, which if true would certainly account for its rather - and perhaps I'm making unfair presumptions here - the rather templated quality of the document, if I can put it that way. That is, Variants A and B read pretty much the same. A lot of military orders tend to be sort of boiler-plate. I think that's the word I was looking for. So that would -- that would account for that. Whether that's true or not, the only indication that we have is from that very late-dated indication from the office of the SDS. But irrespective of who may have drafted it - and clearly somebody drafted it - the other conclusions in our report - and I think that piece of information is consistent with it - indicate that irrespective of who drafted it it was adopted, if you will, accepted, and apparently distributed and implemented by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, your comment about the boiler-plate aspect of this document, that -- it's Mr. Krajisnik's position - and I wonder whether you'd agree with it, then - that the tone and the language - of course, it's written in Serbian - the tone and the language of this document is rather in the style of military, old communist-regime authors. Do you agree with that? Do you --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that could be. I -- I've read a lot of military orders in my day but not a lot of ones written in Serbian, quite frankly, because I don't work in the military area here. So that may well be true, but I couldn't confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. And in particular -- I won't press you too far, because after all, Mr. Krajisnik does have the advantage on this point of being a Serb, and Serbian is his own language. But he -- it's suggested particularly that references to -- whatever the equivalent word is in Serbian here -- to "commander" and the reference to "our armed forces" that in small but cumulative ways the whole language and tone of this document has that old military ring to it. Can you comment on that, Mr. Treanor, or have we got as far as you're really able to --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- go?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I would say, I cannot contest that, and I frankly concede my ignorance on that point. The SDS leadership and the members of the Assembly in particular were very supportive of the JNA, so it doesn't surprise me that they would have been very close to members of the JNA or retired members of the JNA who may have assisted them with various tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, do you consider it likely that Mr. Krajisnik, who was the president of the Serb Assembly and who had chaired that earlier debate in which the recommendation in relation to what I call minority municipalities had been adopted, do you consider it likely that Mr. Krajisnik would have associated himself, then, with a document in the form of this Variant A and B document without any further reference back to the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, the -- as I said earlier, there seems to have been a two-track process going on here: One with the recommendation of the Assembly, which was a public document, that Assemblies of the Serbian People be formed, as opposed to this document, which was an internal party document and distributed through party channels, obviously confidentially since we know so little about it, and which of course goes far beyond simply the establishing of Serbian Assemblies but includes instructions for the establishment of executive organs and other activities, such as the protection of property.
